newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens sees no change in GPT shares.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees no change in GPT shares.

text.p: Britain's General Electric Co Plc and Siemens AG will not make any changes to the shareholdings in their telecommunications joint venture GPT, Siemens said on Tuesday.
Siemens holds around 60 percent of GPT and GEC holds the remaining shares.
Earlier GEC unveiled its long awaited strategic blueprint to take it into the next century, putting defence at the heart of the group and signalling a possible float of its rail/power joint venture.
Managing director George Simpson said GEC is also considering "repositioning" its telecoms joint venture GPT.
Simpson said he had thought about selling the telecoms stake, but rejected it.

"Clearly one option was to sell our stake to Siemens. But I am driven by shareholder value. We will monitor the business and rewrite the charter for that business, as telecoms is a high growth area which GEC should remain in," he said.
